why: searchCandidates runs every candidate through normalizeForSearch, which collapses \s+ (tabs included) to a single space before any query is built — so findClauseRange never issues a query containing a raw tab at all. Verified by spying on body.search against the real, unmodified word.ts: it issues 4 queries for this input, none containing \t (the tab is replaced by a space in every one). Each of those space-joined candidates then fails to match the raw tab-separated document text, so the result is correctly null, but via query normalization, not tab rejection — a two-column signature block target spanning a raw tab genuinely cannot be located this way. A documented limitation, pinned so it cannot change silently. (word.ts's own Rule-8-equivalent tab handling belongs to the fake, not to findClauseRange, and is covered independently by wordFake.test.ts's rule8 assertions.)
